title: FSD S4 reads the ACE views and the batch-status view directly, while Architecture v5 allows only rwb-source-data to read them and the connection matrix gives S4 no cell to P1
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 13, 37 and 45; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1; Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1 DP-05 and DP-13
section: A1.1 constraints; A2.1 to A2.22 integration points and VR-S4-001-1 to VR-S4-022-1; A2.11 integration point
description: The FSD is explicit that source data is read only from the ACE database through the SELECT-only recovery.v_ace_* views, and seventeen of the twenty-two features carry validation rule VR-S4-00n-1 against v_ace_batch_status. A2.11 reads the LIT hearings through ACE and A2.17 reads the NCB. Architecture v5 slide 37 changes '30 views read by any module (ADR-010)' to views read only by rwb-source-data, slide 45 answers 'who reads ACE data' with rwb-source-data alone plus REST or a Temporal activity for everyone else, and slide 13 gives the S4 row a T to P7, a T and E to P6 and a T and E to S9 and no cell to P1 at all. The whole read path of this service is therefore undefined, and the FSD's own rule wording contradicts the platform it is being realigned to.
evidence: FSD S4 A1.1 Constraints; VR-S4-001-1, VR-S4-002-1, VR-S4-004-1, VR-S4-008-1, VR-S4-009-1, VR-S4-011-1, VR-S4-012-1, VR-S4-015-1, VR-S4-016-1, VR-S4-017-1, VR-S4-019-1 and VR-S4-022-1; A2.11.2 'Integration points. LIT, Partner portal' and A2.17.2 'Integration points. NCB, Model gateway'. Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 37, slide 45 (only rwb-source-data reads the 30 views), slide 13 (S4 row: T to P7; T E to P6; T E to S9; no P1 cell). Rules DP-05, DP-10, DP-13.
proposed: Carry the FSD's field names as the source field names that the rwb-source-data contract returns, and build every step on that contract; no view and no ACE table is read by this service. Confirm the contract fields, the LIT view names and the freshness response with P1 before the wave 2 notice test.

title: The connection matrix gives S4 no cell to rwb-document, rwb-payment or rwb-agent, while the FSD names the document hub, ALS and GL and the model gateway
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 13 and 19; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 endpoints
section: A2.4, A2.6, A2.10 field catalogs; A2.6 and A2.4 integration points; A2.15 integration point; A2.12 integration point; A2.22 integration point
description: The FSD's integration points name 'the Workbench document hub' for the pack and the missing document, 'ALS and GL' for the court fee and the legal expense, 'ALS and GL, LED portal' for the enforcement proceeds match, and 'Model gateway' for the next litigation step. Architecture v5 slide 19 gives the S4 contract Temporal edges to Partner (issueInstruction), Comms (demand notice child) and Decision (approval child) and no other edge, and slide 13 gives the S4 row no cell to P5, P8 or P10. The Ownership Map lists only the five S4 REST paths, so no document, payment or agent contract is recorded for this service anywhere in the sources read.
evidence: FSD S4 A2.4.2 and A2.6.2 integration points (the Workbench document hub, CCMS); A2.12.2 ('Workbench, Model gateway'); A2.15.2 ('Partner portal, ALS and GL'); A2.22.2 ('ALS and GL, LED portal'). Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 19 (S4 IN and OUT) and slide 13 (the S4 row). Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 Endpoints: five paths with owner S4, none to P5, P8 or P10.
proposed: Carry the three edges as contract dependencies on the P5, P8 and P10 contract stories and build this service against their published fakes, with the pack, the fee and the agent call behind the contract that the contract story fixes. No direct call and no second writer is introduced by this document.

title: The Ownership Map gives rwb-litigation two tables, while Architecture v5 gives the schema judgments, enforcement and the LED auction ladder and the FSD holds notice, pack and deferral state
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 19, 30 and 41; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 tables; Recovery Workbench FSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) field catalog
section: A2.1 to A2.3 (notice state and served result); A2.16 (judgment); A2.18 to A2.21 (enforcement, ladder, deferral, petition); A2.22 (proceeds)
description: Architecture v5 slide 19 states that rwb-litigation 'writes schema rwb_litigation: legal actions, hearings, judgments, enforcement, LED auction ladder' and slide 41 repeats the same list as what the service owns. The Ownership Map Tables sheet has exactly two rows with owner S4, legal_action and hearing, plus the four platform library objects, and no row for a judgment, an enforcement record, an auction round, a pack, a notice state, a deferral or a decision record. The FSD's field catalog for all twenty-two features repeats the same eight legal_action columns, so the table set the DB story is written from does not exist for six of the eight things the schema is said to hold.
evidence: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 19 (DB writes schema rwb_litigation: legal actions, hearings, judgments, enforcement, LED auction ladder) and slide 41 (S4 owns legal actions, hearings, judgments, enforcement, LED auction ladder). Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 Tables: legal_action (S4), hearing (S4); no other S4 row. FSD S4 A2.6.3.2, A2.7.3.2, A2.10.3.2, A2.13.3.2, A2.14.3.2, A2.18.3.2, A2.20.3.2 and A2.21.3.2 field catalog: the same eight legal_action columns.
proposed: State the six missing entity groups and their key fields as product requirements and fix no physical table name beyond the two the map already holds; the table set and the physical schema are written when the S4 DB story is picked up, and the missing rows are added to the Ownership Map in the same change.

title: legal_action.case_id is a uuid in the FSD, while ADR-014 and DP-01 forbid a cross-schema foreign key and require a varchar(255) business key
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) field catalog; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 20 and 45; Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1 DP-01 and DP-15
description: Every field catalog of the FSD types legal_action.case_id as uuid with the meaning 'The recovery_case this record belongs to' and the required flag Yes, and lists no foreign key. Under Architecture v5 the case lives in schema rwb_case and this service writes only schema rwb_litigation, so a uuid column carrying a cross-schema reference is exactly what DP-01 forbids; the platform pattern is a business-key column of type varchar(255) with no foreign key. The same column is the key of almost every entity in this schema, so the DB story cannot start until it is settled.
evidence: FSD S4 A2.6.3.2 to A2.21.3.2 field catalog row 'legal_action.case_id | The recovery_case this record belongs to | uuid | Yes | None | No'. Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 20 (schema and login per service) and slide 45. Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1 DP-01 (never read another service's tables) and DP-15 (per-service Flyway in the service's own schema). ADR-014.
proposed: Use a business-key column of type varchar(255) with no foreign key, keeping the FSD's field name; the case number is the business key and no identifier of another schema is stored as a foreign key.

title: The notice and its proof of delivery sit in S4 in the FSD and in rwb-comms in Architecture v5 and the Ownership Map, and the three notice paths are split across the two services
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) A2.1 to A2.3; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 endpoints and services
section: A2.1, A2.2, A2.3 (generation, proof of delivery, notice period); Screens SCR-18
description: The FSD gives module S4 the demand and recall notice, its approval, the proof of delivery and the notice period, and its own integration points name WIN for dispatch. Architecture v5 slide 41 gives rwb-comms 'notices, templates, merge fields, proof of delivery', and the Ownership Map therefore puts POST /cases/{caseId}/notices and GET /notices/{noticeId} on P6 while POST /notices/{noticeId}/approve is x-module S4, on the same resource. Two services appear to own the notice, its state and its served result, and the notice period cannot start from a proof of delivery that this service does not hold.
evidence: FSD S4 A1.2 FEAT-LIT-01 to FEAT-LIT-03; A2.1.2 integration point 'WIN, Workbench'; A2.2.2 integration point 'WIN'; A2.2.3.1 R-LIT-07, R-LIT-08, R-LIT-09; Screens SCR-18 notice approval, first in E2. Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41 (rwb-comms owns notices, templates, merge fields, proof of delivery). Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 Endpoints: POST /cases/{caseId}/notices (P6), GET /notices/{noticeId} (P6), POST /notices/{noticeId}/approve (S4).
proposed: This service decides that a notice is due, approves it and owns the notice period; rwb-comms owns the template, the merge fields, the delivery and the proof of delivery, and returns the served result as NoticeDelivered. The notice period starts from the delivered_at that rwb-comms returns, and the notice state on the case is written by this service only.

title: The notice capability is first needed in Epic 2 (wave 2, 31 December 2026 (tentative)) while the service is created in wave 3
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) module table and Screens; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5 section 8 and 10.2; Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1 R5.6
section: Document control module table; Screens SCR-18
description: The FSD's module table reads 'S4 | Litigation and enforcement | E2 notices; E5' and its screens list gives SCR-18 notice approval the first-in E2. The Program BRD release plan puts E2 at 31 December 2026 (tentative) and E5 at 31 March 2027 (tentative), and section 10.2 puts RWB-SVC-S4 in wave 3. The wave map in R5.6 puts EP02 in wave 2 and EP05 in wave 3, and R5.6 also says a story whose wave map wave is earlier than its service's wave keeps the wave map wave, so notice work is due one wave before the service that owns it exists.
evidence: FSD S4 document control module table ('S4 | Litigation and enforcement | E2 notices; E5') and Screens ('SCR-18 Notice approval | Generated demand and recall notices for approval before dispatch | E2'). Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5 section 8 (E2 31 Dec 2026 (tentative), E5 31 Mar 2027 (tentative)) and section 10.2 (RWB-SVC-S4, wave 3). Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1 R5.6 wave map and the conflict rule.
proposed: Publish the notice contract, its fake and its schema as slice 2.1 before wave 3, let the notice stories keep the EP02 wave 2 that R5.6 gives them, and build the rest of the capability in wave 3 against the same contract.

title: Thirty-two of the seventy-nine R-LIT rules are named in the FSD and the litigation rule package is Phase 2
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) A2.1 to A2.22 rule tables; Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 20 and slide 48; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1 BR-034 source column
section: A2.1.3.1 to A2.22.3.1; slide 20 of the Drools design
description: The FSD's rule tables name R-LIT-03, 04, 07, 08, 09, 11, 15, 16, 18, 21, 23, 24, 26, 27, 28, 30, 31, 32, 36, 37, 38, 44, 45, 50, 51, 52, 54, 55, 58, 65, 67 and 70, thirty-two of the seventy-nine the BRD cites as R-LIT-01 to R-LIT-79. The remaining forty-seven (R-LIT-01, 02, 05, 06, 10, 12, 13, 14, 17, 19, 20, 22, 25, 29, 33, 34, 35, 39 to 43, 46 to 49, 53, 56, 57, 59 to 64, 66, 68, 69 and 71 to 79) are named in no FSD section, including the two the design relies on for the prescription escalation (R-LIT-20) and the broken settlement (R-LIT-40 is named only in the Drools design). The Drools design says the litigation set is 79 rules and the package is Phase 2, so the rule base the requirements are tested against does not exist yet.
evidence: FSD S4 A2.1.3.1 to A2.22.3.1 rule ID column; the twelve distinct rules repeated across features. Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 20 ('Litigation route set, 79 rules (package Phase 2)', 'R-LIT-63 to 67', 'R-LIT-11/20', 'R-LIT-57', 'R-LIT-40') and the Phase 2 open point (Drools packages for S1 and S3 to S9). Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1 BR-034 source column ('R-LIT-01 to R-LIT-79').
proposed: Take the thirty-two rules the FSD names as the requirement set of this PRD, treat the other forty-seven as authoring work for the package, and require the package code, its version label and its owner in rwb-decision before the wave 3 release. No rule is restated here and no value is invented.

title: Every FSD acceptance criterion is the same generic sentence and there is no alternate flow and no background event for any of the twenty-two features
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) A2.1.4 to A2.22.4
description: Each of the twenty-two main-success criteria reads 'The data and rules it needs are in place / The trigger arrives / The result is recorded with its rule version', and the two exception criteria of each feature read 'Refused with MSG-P4-002; nothing changes' and 'Nothing changes; MSG-P7-003; incident raised'. Every alternate-flow table says 'No alternate path' and every system-background-event table says 'No background event', although A2.3 is a timer, A2.11 tracks a court calendar and A2.19 follows an auction ladder. The consequence is that no source criterion states a business outcome, so the criteria in this PRD are written from the rules each feature names and each one cites the FSD row it comes from.
evidence: FSD S4 A2.1.4.1 to A2.22.4.1 (main success flow, the identical three-column statement), A2.1.4.2 to A2.22.4.2 ('None | No alternate path') and A2.1.4.4 to A2.22.4.4 ('None | No background event').
proposed: Read each FSD row as one criterion per feature and write the step-specific criterion from the rules that feature names, with the FSD row cited as its evidence. The story-level scenarios are written in the story files with their origin tag, as R7.2 requires.

title: LawsuitFiled, JudgmentRecorded and AuctionResult have no EV number and no catalogue row
source: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 19, 42 and 43; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 events
section: Slide 19 S4 OUT; slides 42 and 43 event catalogue
description: Architecture v5 slide 19 gives the S4 OUT contract 'rwb.litigation.events.v1: LawsuitFiled, JudgmentRecorded, AuctionResult', but the event catalogue on slides 42 and 43 has no numbered row for any of the three: JudgmentRecorded and AuctionResult appear only as the unnumbered '+' row at the end of slide 43, and LawsuitFiled appears on slide 19 alone. The Ownership Map events sheet holds none of the three, so a consumer cannot be wired to a contract row and the reporting read model cannot subscribe by name.
evidence: Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 19 (OUT: rwb.litigation.events.v1: LawsuitFiled, JudgmentRecorded, AuctionResult); slide 43 (the last row is '| + | JudgmentRecorded, AuctionResult | rwb-litigation | rwb.litigation.events.v1 | rwb-asset, rwb-case |'). Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 Events: no row with owner S4.
proposed: Carry the three event names, the topic and the consumers as the contract, keyed by the case, and leave the EV numbers to the event catalogue change. No EV id is asserted here.

title: R-LIT-01 starts litigation on route R4 while the case journeys call R4 the guarantee claim and R5 litigation
source: Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 20 and open points; Recovery Workbench FSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) A1.1
section: S4 open point; the route the legal action starts from
description: The Drools design says 'R-LIT-01 starts litigation on route = R4' and, in the same document's open points, that 'Case Journeys v3 calls R4 the guarantee claim and R5 litigation'. The FSD's S4 scope begins at the notices and never names a route number, so the route a legal action starts from is stated one way in the design and another way in the case journeys. The route number drives the route decision that starts LitigationWorkflow, so the trigger of the whole service is ambiguous.
evidence: Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 20 notes ('Starts when litigation route approved (R-LIT-01), or a restructure or settlement plan breaks (R-LIT-02)') and the open point 'Route numbering: R-LIT-01 starts litigation on route = R4; Case Journeys v3 calls R4 the guarantee claim and R5 litigation'. FSD S4 A1.1 scope.
proposed: Name no route number in this document: the legal action starts when the route decision names litigation or when a restructure or settlement plan breaks (R-LIT-01, R-LIT-02), and the numbering is settled in rwb-decision as reference data.

title: REQ-S4-009 (prescription warnings) has no BRD requirement row, and BR-038 and BR-042 carry no program requirement ID
source: Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5 section 5.11; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1 section 8.3; Recovery Workbench FSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) Requirements served
section: Program BRD 5.11; Epics 3 to 8 BR-034 to BR-043
description: The program BRD states ten requirements for S4, REQ-S4-001 to REQ-S4-010, all Must. The E5 requirement set maps them as REQ-S4-001 to BR-034, REQ-S4-002 to BR-035, REQ-S4-003 to BR-036, REQ-S4-004 to BR-037, REQ-S4-005 to BR-039, REQ-S4-006 to BR-040, REQ-S4-007 and REQ-S4-008 to BR-041 and REQ-S4-010 to BR-043. REQ-S4-009, 'Prescription warnings force a litigation review ahead of every other open action on the case', has no row; its rule family appears only inside BR-034's source column. In the other direction BR-038 (court filing and receipt matched to the LIT lawsuit) and BR-042 (asset trace, writ, ladder and bankruptcy petition) carry no program requirement ID. A reader cannot tell whether the BRD lost a requirement or the mapping did.
evidence: Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5 section 5.11 (REQ-S4-001 to REQ-S4-010). Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1 section 8.3 BR-034 (sources REQ-S4-001, REQ-APD-006), BR-035, BR-036, BR-037, BR-038 (no REQ), BR-039 (REQ-S4-005), BR-040 (REQ-S4-006), BR-041 (REQ-S4-007, REQ-S4-008), BR-042 (no REQ), BR-043 (REQ-S4-010).
proposed: Carry REQ-S4-009 into this PRD as FR-S4-051 and FR-S4-052 under BR-034, the requirement that owns the statutory clock, and record the gap so the E5 BRD can add the row. Carry BR-038 and BR-042 from the FSD features and the RWB-E5 story keys. Nothing is dropped and no requirement is merged.

title: The three S4 screens have no owner cell in the v5 screen matrix, and SCR-18's first-in is Epic 2
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) Screens; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41 and the edge slides; Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1 endpoints
description: The FSD lists three screens for this module: SCR-18 notice approval (first in E2), SCR-19 litigation workspace and SCR-20 enforcement workspace (first in E5). Architecture v5 slide 41 gives the service catalogue and the edge and gateway design gives composite routes, but neither states which service each screen belongs to, and the Ownership Map lists the API paths only. The composite route that serves a screen joins more than one service here, because SCR-19 shows the pack from rwb-document, the court dates from this service and the case party from rwb-case.
evidence: FSD S4 Screens: SCR-18 notice approval (E2), SCR-19 litigation workspace (E5), SCR-20 enforcement workspace (E5). Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41 (edge and gateway) and the gateway-bff composite route; Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1 DP-19.
proposed: Serve the three screens from gateway-bff composite routes and let this service answer the legal-action part of each; the screen owner cell is recorded with the edge work and is not decided here.

title: The message wording and the Thai and English versions of the S4 messages are not in the FSD
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) A2.1.3.1 to A2.22.3.1; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5 DL10 and DL59
section: Every validation rule row that names a message
description: The FSD names MSG-P1-001, MSG-P4-002, MSG-P7-003, MSG-GEN-001, MSG-S4-001 and MSG-S4-002 and gives one English wording for each, but gives no Thai wording, no field-level text for MSG-GEN-001 and no owner for the wording. The Program BRD leaves the Thai name of every field, label and message to DL10, and NFR-059 requires every label and message in Thai and in English. The two messages that carry a business meaning here, MSG-S4-001 'The pack is missing {item}.' and MSG-S4-002 'The claim on this case expires on {date}.', decide what the officer reads at the moment of filing.
evidence: FSD S4 A2.5.3.1 VR-S4-005-1 (MSG-S4-001), A2.3.3.1 VR-S4-003-1 (MSG-S4-002), A2.14.3.1 VR-S4-014-1 (MSG-GEN-001), A2.1.3.1 VR-S4-001-1 (MSG-P1-001), A2.6.3.1 VR-S4-006-2 (MSG-P4-002), A2.1.4.3 AC-EXC-S4-001-02 (MSG-P7-003). Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5 DL10; NFR-059.
proposed: Preserve the message IDs and the English wording of the FSD character for character, and leave the Thai wording, the field-level text and the approver to the message work DL10 names.

title: The sources state no litigation, hearing or enforcement volume for this module, and no release date other than the program release plan
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S4 Litigation and enforcement v3 (03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6) A1.2 and A2.1.1 to A2.22.1; Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5 section 8; Non Functional Specification v3 sections 2 and 3
section: A2.1.1 to A2.22.1 metric tables; NFR-001, NFR-002, NFR-003
description: Every one of the twenty-two features carries the same single metric, 'Litigation turnaround | 21 days | 6 days' (the FSD writes the target as 6 days), and no feature states a case count, a hearing count, a filing count or an enforcement count. The non-functional specification gives the case store volume (about 23,600 open cases at go-live), the staff population (about 370 of 914 online) and the partner population (about 50 of about 320 online, across 11 to 12 law firms), none of which is split by module. A performance target for this service therefore has no module-specific volume behind it, and the release date used in this document is the program release plan date and nothing else.
evidence: FSD S4 A2.1.1 to A2.22.1 metric table ('Litigation turnaround | 6 days'). Non Functional Specification v3 NFR-001, NFR-002, NFR-003, NFR-007. Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v5 section 8 release plan (E2 31 Dec 2026 (tentative), E5 31 Mar 2027 (tentative)).
proposed: Use the population figures the non-functional specification states, mark the litigation share as open, and copy every release date unchanged and tentative. No volume and no date is invented here.
